Method of Attack: Abuses the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to duplicate access tokens for privilege escalation to SYSTEM level
Uses WFP ALE kernel-mode layers and device IO requests to duplicate SYSTEM tokens without calling DuplicateHandle for stealth
Triggers IPSec connection and abuses Print Spooler service to insert SYSTEM token into the token table
Abuses OneSyncSvc service and SyncController.dll to obtain tokens of other logged-in users for lateral movement
Attack Vector: Abuse of Windows Filtering Platform API and kernel-mode drivers
RPC calls to Print Spooler and OneSyncSvc services
Device IO requests to WfpAle kernel-mode layers
IPSec policy configuration and local host RPC connections
Indicators of Compromise: Configuring new IPSec policies that don’t match known network configuration
RPC calls to Spooler / OneSyncSvc while IPSec policy is active
Multiple calls to WfpAleQueryTokenById to brute force LUID of a token
Device IO requests to WfpAle by processes other than the BFE service
